name: room2-demos-ab-v1
status: Training plan. Written by the worker during a 16-hour autonomous window the owner granted on 2026-09-24 after choosing O2 option 3. Training may start before the orchestrator reviews this plan (owner-authorized use of idle compute; if the review changes the design, the runs are repeated). No held-out evaluation before that review: the evaluation plan is committed only after it.
question: Does fine-tuning from a clone fitted on more demonstration routes improve Room 2 held-out success over fine-tuning from the current clone, across eight matched seeds, on the fresh v2 held-out set?
why: The noise check came back null (Objective 5): sampling noise is not the main cost. Most remaining failures are at the pit and spike crossing (916 of 1,136 stochastic failures in the noise check ended at x 360 to 459), which every demonstration crosses by bouncing off a spring the observation grid cannot see. The current clone learned that crossing from 5 fitted routes. More routes through the same crossing give the clone, and so both the starting policy and fine-tuning, more varied examples of it. A critic warm-up was considered and set aside: in the 12 earlier runs the critic recovered within 3 to 5 updates and early success stayed at the clone's level.
expected_effect: No prior estimate exists for Room 2. Demonstrations were the largest lever in Room 1 (no clears without them, 84% canonical after fine-tuning with seven). With eight seeds the exact sign-flip test can reach p <= 0.05 only if at least 7 of 8 seed differences share a sign and, given the earlier per-seed spread of about 6 points, reliably detects roughly an 8 to 10 point route-macro effect; arm A's earlier level (86.8% on the old set) leaves about 13 points of headroom. A smaller true effect will most likely read as inconclusive.

arm_B_demonstrations.new_route_search: seeds 7 to 20 in runs/room2-routes, each tried once with --max-minutes 10; every route found is used, none chosen by hand; log runs/demo-search/20260924-013144/search.log

arm_A_clone.split: 5 routes fitted, 2 held out for clone validation (2406 and 858 frames)

arm_B_clone.split: 16 routes fitted, 5 held out for clone validation (7520 and 2275 frames)
arm_B_clone.procedure: scripts/clone_room1.py with the arm A clone's recorded settings (routes only, holdout 0.25, 300 epochs, batch 64, learning rate 0.001, seed 0, no play) and --heldout config/heldout_starts-room2-v2.json, so the overlap guard checks the set this experiment is evaluated on

source.clones_on_canonical_start_descriptive: Training-side, measured before any fine-tuning with evaluate_checkpoint.py, 50 stochastic canonical-start episodes, sampling seed 20260924: arm A clone 10/50 (the noise check's clone reference run, runs/evaluation/chapter-1-room-2/20260923-210315), arm B clone 5/50 (95% interval 4.3% to 21.4%; runs/evaluation/chapter-1-room-2/20260924-015734). Not a basis for any decision here.

training_protocol.order: A then B within each seed, ascending seed order
training_protocol.start_sampling: canonical start only, in both arms
training_protocol.checkpoint_selection: Final latest.zip from each declared run, after the requested budget. Never best.zip. No checkpoint selection using held-out results. If a run is missing, do not replace it or analyze a subset.
training_protocol.resumed_runs: run_overnight.py retries a failed run once with --resume. A resumed run is valid but not bit-reproducible (random states are not restored); it is included and flagged.
training_protocol.clone_use: Copy the arm's cloned policy weights into every run with a fresh optimizer and the run's seed.
training_protocol.code_identity: Training runs at the commit that adds this plan, on a clean tree; run_overnight.py records that commit in the campaign summary and every run records it in its manifest. The evaluation plan will pin the commit it runs at as well as the tool blob, because a tool blob cannot see changes to the modules it imports.

training_health_descriptive.rule: Reported for every run; never used to exclude or replace a run.
metrics: canonical-start clears in the final 10% of each run's training episodes
timeout share of training episodes per 100,000-transition window
faults summed over every session, including sessions[].rolled_back.fault_stats_before
one deterministic canonical-start episode per saved step checkpoint (evaluate_checkpoint.py, training side, never held-out), as a stall detector
policy entropy from progress.csv at each 100,000-transition window

evaluation_protocol.checkpoint_hashes: After training, and only after the orchestrator has reviewed this plan, hash every declared final latest.zip and commit a mechanically completed evaluation plan before any held-out evaluation. Evaluate each checkpoint once. Nothing has ever been evaluated on this set.

arms.A: fine-tuning from the current clone (7 routes)
arms.B: fine-tuning from the new clone (21 routes)

analysis.primary_estimand: Within each matched seed, calculate success proportion per complete-route hash and average the twelve route rates equally. Average the eight paired B-minus-A differences equally.
analysis.primary_test: Exact two-sided paired sign-flip test over eight seed-level route-macro B-minus-A differences, enumerating all 256 assignments.
analysis.interval: 95% percentile crossed-cluster bootstrap, independently resampling matched seed pairs and complete-route clusters with replacement while retaining A/B pairing and all states within a selected route.
analysis.decision_rule: Evidence favouring B requires a positive primary estimate, a 95% crossed-cluster interval excluding zero, and exact two-sided paired p <= 0.05. Evidence against B requires the mirror image. Otherwise inconclusive.
analysis.missingness: Fail closed for any absent run, changed checkpoint or artifact hash, missing or duplicated state row, or replay problem. Never use complete cases or select alternate checkpoints.

analysis_code.note: Unchanged committed analyzer, run on the mechanically completed evaluation plan with --output to a new path.

secondary_descriptive: per-arm route-macro and state-weighted success; per-seed and per-route differences (analyzer output)
the 500,000-step result is the only held-out measurement; earlier step checkpoints stay training-side
failures by end_x band (before 360, 360 to 459, after 459), per arm

definitions.heldout_cluster: complete search route identified by its full-route SHA-256
definitions.reason_not_to_use_binomial_intervals: States from one route are adjacent trajectory prefixes and all checkpoints use the same frozen starts.
definitions.v2_overlap: Descriptive, computed before any training. Against arm A's 7 routes: 16 of the 200 v2 states share (task frame, position, dashes) with a demonstration state, all at task frames 20 to 44. Against arm B's 21 routes: 19, of which 16 at task frames 20 to 44 and 3 later (frame 104 at (341, -24), frame 128 at (348, -24), both 1 dash, standing near the pillar; frame 452 at (540, -97), 0 dashes, in the exit shaft), all 3 from new routes. Matching frame, position and dashes does not make the states identical (velocity and recent inputs can differ). No v2 route shares even one opening input with any of the 21 demonstrations. The 3 extra coincidences could favour arm B slightly; they are disclosed, not removed.
